description: The OpenMesh team at Columbia University and Tel Aviv University publishes tools for deriving urban rainfall information from wireless-link attenuation. Python modules fetch and read mesh-network observations and weather-station data, then preprocess and analyse them through documented notebooks. The reference application covers New York City from October 2023 to July 2024 using one-minute communications measurements. GitHub provides setup guidance for Python 3.11 or 3.12, while Zenodo archives version 1.1.0 under CC-BY-4.0; both offer free public access. Optional Weather Underground acquisition needs a separate key, but the archived default data can support review and reproduction without obtaining that service. Link behaviour and non-weather attenuation create uncertainty in rainfall estimates. The workflow can prepare rainfall forcing or validation series for urban drainage simulations. It complements the OpenMesh dataset by exposing processing and comparison with independent weather stations. Nothing was installed, downloaded or executed.
